criterion_scale.0.5: Partially satisfied but incomplete or weakly evidenced.
criterion_scale.1: Fully satisfied with evidence from the response, trace, diff, or artifacts.

criteria.description: Identifies that randperm operated on a process-local batch before AutoParallel but would permute the global logical batch after capture.
Raises a clear SPMD modeling warning with the affected location and semantic risk instead of treating successful tracing as proof of correctness.
Proposes preserving replica and local-batch structure or using the independent permutation construct before flattening.
Does not edit the model and asks the user to confirm the intended stochastic semantics before a non-trivial adaptation.
Considers a 1D baseline and a small 2D candidate set without enumerating every factorization.
Recommends the topology-aligned (2, 8) candidate with the inner dimension mapped to the intra-node fast domain.
Does not recommend a mesh with more than two dimensions and relates that limit to ILP solve cost.
Checks model-dimension divisibility, DP batch compatibility, and rank layout before treating the mesh as valid.
Labels the mesh as an inferred optimization hypothesis and proposes independent plan comparisons.
States that visible GPUs do not establish the intended world size or node allocation.
Asks for the intended GPU count and node topology or a launch configuration before planning.
Does not capture, solve, or recommend an eight-GPU mesh based only on nvidia-smi output.
Selects a 1D eight-GPU mesh as the planning mesh.
Does not recommend running a 2D candidate without a concrete memory, semantic-axis, compute-parallel, or link-locality benefit.
Notes that an unnecessary 2D mesh expands placement representation or solver search cost without a topology advantage on one NVSwitch domain.
Uses ShardingOptimizer.load on the trusted artifact and does not attempt CPU graph capture.
Finds the requested node in the saved optimizer graph and uses its stable name directly.
Shows add constraint, resolve, diff, remove returned constraint names, and resolve again to restore the baseline state.
Does not lower, compile, benchmark, modify the artifact, or claim target execution evidence.
Notes that non-ATen custom operations may need registration modules available when loading.
Keeps one topology configuration active across planning, compilation, and metrics, and passes collector.cost_model to AutoParallel.
Uses the collector's post-grad scheduler and disables overlap scheduling in autoparallel_backend.
Runs forward and backward before leaving the collector context so lazy backward compilation is observed.
Requires forward and backward records and writes the collector JSON artifact.
Calls the results estimated rather than measured and keeps them separate from ILP objective values.
Notes that the current AutoParallel pass does not insert overlap control dependencies, so later Inductor scheduling or fusion may move the measured order.
Changes only the isolated harness and does not add or modify a public AutoParallel API.
Removes the exploratory node-constraint names and resolves before changing intended deployment constraints.
Tests output and memory constraints separately rather than dropping both at once.
Records which specific relaxation restores feasibility and does not present the relaxed plan as the original deployment.
Reuses the stable optimizer graph and does not retrace or lower during diagnosis.
Treats the undiscounted and zero-discount results as pessimistic and optimistic placement endpoints, deduplicates placement families, and does not recommend a broad discount sweep.
States that free prefetch communication is an optimistic sensitivity assumption rather than an executable performance prediction.
Preserves the two endpoint placements as distinct artifacts for later lowering and does not claim that discount calls compound or require recapture.

Separates persistent parameter placement from heavy-operation compute placement and flags latency-sensitive inter-node TP as topology inversion requiring investigation rather than automatic acceptance or forced reversal.

Proposes lowering only distinct candidates with the same NCCL topology, activation-checkpointing, and autobucketing configuration, then comparing forward/backward exposed communication and peak memory.
Reports achieved byte-weighted parameter storage, distinguishes it from total training or transient memory, and checks effective DP degree and local batch.
Returns a provisional candidate set or confidence card when endpoint placements differ instead of claiming one ILP result is the final optimum.
States that GPU count does not define global batch and that the synthetic local-batch-one smoke point is not representative quality evidence.

Does not infer missing propagation rules from selected placements alone and proposes distinguishing replicate-only option sets and implicit fallbacks from replicated choices with sharded alternatives.
Does not silently invent or enlarge the missing production microbatch and does not transfer a result from a larger synthetic batch to production routing.
Proposes at most one or two larger local-microbatch points for a controlled sensitivity experiment, holds the remaining execution contract fixed, and uses an aligned baseline for each point.
Limits the original run to smoke or workload-sensitivity evidence and requests the real training configuration before making a production strategy decision.
Uses global batch 96 for the global logical AutoParallel capture input rather than substituting world size or another benchmark batch.
Derives and uses local batch 12 for execution from global batch 96 divided by the eight-way DP degree.
Checks divisibility and keeps the reported global batch, captured input shape, effective DP degree, and executed local shape consistent.
Treats any different batch as a separately reported sensitivity configuration and does not use it in place of the specified batch-96 evaluation.
Adds the two absent local FP32 AdamW moment tensors: 8 GiB for AutoParallel and 4 GiB for FSDP, without double-counting parameters or gradients already present at the measured boundary.
Projects AutoParallel to 82 GiB before operational reserve and therefore rejects its otherwise faster result under the 80 GiB production limit.
Projects FSDP to 59 GiB before reserve and selects it as the feasible fallback, subject to the same remaining acceptance checks.
Labels latency and forward/backward peak as measured, optimizer-state memory as analytical, and records OPTIMIZER_STATE_MEMORY_INFEASIBLE rather than calling the projected peak measured.
Notes that the complete production decision must also reserve explicit operational headroom instead of accepting an exact-capacity fit.
Does not accept AutoParallel for production training speed from a forward/loss/backward-only latency win when optimizer update cost is missing.
Explains that parameter placement changes optimizer work and DTensor dispatch overhead, so the full-step ranking may differ.
Treats end-to-end competitiveness as inconclusive or comparison_unavailable with OPTIMIZER_PERFORMANCE_UNMODELED or STEP_BOUNDARY_MISMATCH.
Preserves the working DDP integration until aligned full-step evidence meets the acceptance bar.
Requests aligned AdamW-step measurements or a versioned held-out-calibrated optimizer-cost envelope for both strategies with the same optimizer implementation and settings.
Does not diagnose missing sharding propagation merely from the selected placements because 98% of tensor nodes exposed sharded alternatives.
Explains that the current sharding objective prices forward/backward but not placement-dependent eager optimizer update work, so retaining more local parameters can reverse the full-step ranking.
Selects measured optimizer-inclusive FSDP because it is faster and smaller for the intended production boundary.

Records OPTIMIZER_COST_MISSING_FROM_OBJECTIVE and preserves the supplied numeric parameter-storage fractions plus the supplied partial- and full-boundary results for improvement work. Exact latency or memory values are not present in the prompt and must not be invented; preserving the stated qualitative win/loss and memory ordering is full credit.
Recognizes that the model is applicable only because hardware, framework, dtype policy, and realized optimizer kernel family match its calibrated regime.
Carries the 14% maximum relevant prospective error into the latency envelope instead of relying on winner accuracy or the 6% point-estimate advantage.
Does not accept AutoParallel because a 6% modeled advantage is not robust to the calibrated error envelope; keeps DDP and labels the result inconclusive or schedule-sensitive.
Labels the comparison modeled rather than measured and asks for aligned full-step evidence if a stronger decision is needed.
Computes approximately 110 seconds for AutoParallel and 70 seconds for DDP over 1,000 steps, including startup and steady-state execution.
Selects DDP for the specified 1,000-step job even though AutoParallel has higher steady-state throughput.
Reports a 5,000-step break-even from the 50-second startup difference divided by the 10 ms per-step saving.
Separates time-to-ready from steady-state step latency, labels the finite-job totals as projected or derived, and does not call all startup time compiler-only time.
Explains that tight iteration samples inside one process do not measure process-launch, compilation, allocator, or system-state variance.
Does not call the 3% single-launch result robustly competitive or switch the production integration from that evidence.
Classifies the result as schedule-sensitive or inconclusive and records MEASURED_LAUNCH_VARIANCE_UNMODELED.
Requests independent launches of both strategies under the same configuration and a combined launch-level envelope or distribution.
Recognizes that FSDP is robustly better on complete-step latency, peak memory, and time-to-ready rather than treating the 5% tolerance as an AutoParallel win.
Selects native FSDP for production unless the user explicitly accepts a different documented tradeoff.
Classifies AutoParallel as Pareto-dominated or below the relative-quality bar rather than robustly competitive.
Uses the stated independent-launch and complete-step evidence rather than inventing a weighted score, and does not claim stronger uncertainty evidence than the prompt provides.
Separates uncertainty in the historical forward/backward base from the validated optimizer increment instead of treating the entire composed prediction as below 1% error.
Does not accept AutoParallel because the 8% point-estimate advantage is inside the applicable 15% base-drift uncertainty.
Classifies the comparison as schedule-sensitive or inconclusive and preserves the existing FSDP integration.

Requests contemporaneous independent-launch partial-step measurements, or a validated temporal-drift envelope, before recomposing the full-step estimate and uses COMPOSED_FULL_STEP_BASE_DRIFT when a refreshed control explains the miss.
Labels the meta result as modeled candidate-ranking evidence rather than measured runtime evidence.
Uses the applicable 68% maximum held-out error rather than the 10% median, so the 20% point-estimate advantage is not robust.
Keeps the existing FSDP integration and classifies AutoParallel as inconclusive or schedule-sensitive instead of accepting it for production.
Uses meta execution for legality, memory and scale exploration, candidate ranking, and prioritizing target measurements, and requests a regime-matched bound or aligned target run for routing.
Computes the AutoParallel accumulation cycle as 3 * 85 + 100 + 40 = 395 ms, or 98.75 ms amortized per microstep.
Computes the DDP accumulation cycle as 3 * 70 + 140 + 20 = 370 ms, or 92.5 ms amortized per microstep.
Selects DDP for the actual update cycle even though AutoParallel's isolated synchronized-microstep-plus-update sum is lower.

Reports the full accumulation cycle, preserving three no-sync microsteps, one synchronized microstep, and one optimizer update rather than multiplying the wrong boundary; any amortized value must use that cycle.
Records no-sync frequency and uses static_graph=false for compiled DDP when synchronization alternates, unless that exact static-graph template has already executed successfully.
Explains that the finalized bundle is durable and not lost; the catalog is a derived snapshot that can lag it.
Does not treat report finalization as catalog publication and calls for refresh_report_feedback.py as a one-shot handoff or a cluster-supervised --watch process.

Checks feedback-status-v1.json for a successful non-stale refresh, verifies the run ID appears in the rebuilt catalog, and checks the rebuilt queue inputs without requiring the run to become a queue candidate.
Keeps finalized report bundles immutable and allows only the refresh workflow to rebuild the derived catalog, queue, and health files.
Treats two- and four-GPU meshes as different routing contracts with different decision IDs rather than letting the newer report supersede the target mesh.
Selects FSDP for the requested two-GPU production deployment because that mesh's replicated evidence Pareto-dominates AutoParallel.
Explains that changing world size changes local batch, collective scale, and potentially the optimized placement, so timing evidence cannot be pooled across meshes.

Requires an explicit NCCL topology describing the allocated two-rank H100 NVSwitch communicator when canonical eight-GPU detection cannot represent the sub-allocation, rather than accepting a fallback cost model or pretending unused GPUs are ranks.
Does not accept AutoParallel from the unclipped timing and labels production competitiveness inconclusive or comparison unavailable.
Requires the same global-L2 clipping algorithm, max norm 1.0, placement after backward and before optimizer.step, and update frequency for AutoParallel and DDP.
Includes clipping's local norm work and any global reduction in the complete measured or modeled step boundary for each placement.
Treats the clipped production contract as distinct from the unclipped report while keeping exact retries and baselines linked under the clipped decision ID.
Rejects the AutoParallel run as a semantic failure because lowering changed the trainability mask and optimizer membership; does not use its timing for production routing.
Selects the executed DDP integration while AutoParallel is fixed and re-evaluated under the exact fine-tuning contract.
Requires a per-FQN requires-grad and optimizer-group invariant after lowering or wrapping before execution evidence is accepted.
For FP32 AdamW, counts 2.24 GB of persistent parameters plus gradient and two moment copies only for the 50 MB trainable subset: 2.24 GB + 3 * 0.05 GB = 2.39 GB, before activations and headroom.
Treats the warned block-wrapped FSDP result as performance-only and does not select it from latency despite it being fastest.
Selects DDP as the correctness-qualified fallback because it is warning-free, feasible, and faster than the warning-free root-only FSDP template.
Records qualification per FSDP template rather than declaring all FSDP infeasible for T5; preserves both the warned block result and safe root-only result with distinct template identities.
Retains the prompt's relative latency and memory-feasibility evidence for root-only FSDP and notes that any new warning-free template must retain its real startup, memory, and copy costs.
Classifies the selected plan as ILP-feasible but failed during placement application, and does not claim successful AutoParallel execution or performance.
Identifies loss of the logical global shape or stride when reconstructing the uneven local shard, including the shorter final rank rather than assuming every rank has the ceiling-sized extent.
Uses the lowering replicated counterfactual to isolate a sharded realizability problem without silently selecting it or treating it as production performance evidence.

Requires preserving logical metadata or excluding the specific unrealizable placement, then checks placement application on long and short ranks plus output shapes, values, and gradients against an unsharded reference.
Treats the incompatible tied-weight placements and runtime shape error as a semantic or execution failure, not usable performance evidence.
Requires source-identity alias groups to share one compatible persistent placement rather than optimizing the two FQNs independently.
Checks after lowering that both FQNs remain the same runtime Parameter with a compatible placement and local shape, then validates outputs and gradients against the tied reference.
Requires a fresh AutoParallel evaluation under the exact tied-weight contract after the fix and, when production routing is in scope, retains a qualified native fallback.
Distinguishes the successful solve from the placement-application alias failure and makes no execution or performance claim.
Maps registered aliases through one canonical captured descriptor and preserves one shared runtime buffer rather than cloning or independently placing state.
Requires aliased observer state to preserve shared identity, placement, mutation, update, and serialization semantics rather than merely avoiding the lookup error.
Calls for a minimized alias regression plus successful apply and QAT execution, shared state-update checks, and comparison with the unpartitioned reference.
Explains that repeated-subgraph clustering compresses the ILP and that the unclustered retry establishes only a feasible unclustered plan, not lowering or production success.
Requires validating a complete correspondence group before linking, skipping a malformed group atomically with diagnostics rather than aborting or disabling all clustering.
Compares feasible placement families and objective under the same constraints and cost model, while recording skipped groups, solve time, and ILP compression counts.
Still requires placement application and later correctness or target evidence before routing; it does not promote the retry from planning evidence.
States that the process-local shuffle and explicit collectives do not directly express the required global logical SPMD computation, so planning is not ready as-is.
Identifies the rank-local shuffle and explicit gathers and explains the local-versus-global semantic risk instead of mechanically deleting collectives or enlarging the batch.
Requests the intended independent-per-rank versus global shuffle semantics before a non-trivial rewrite and requires equivalence validation after any authorized adaptation.

When semantics cannot be expressed directly, proposes an explicit local boundary with internal communication called unpriced, or preserves a qualified native fallback without claiming AutoParallel performance.
Does not invoke or recommend AutoParallel planning, meshes, ILP placement, DTensor sharding, or the skill's collector.
Provides a focused single-GPU profiling and pointwise-kernel optimization sequence.
